views.name: users_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation
FROM users
views.description: Canonical user rows with primary identity and key numeric/text fields useful for ranking or filtering users.
validated_on: What is the display name of the user who last edited the post "Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation"?

views.name: users_public_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.Location AS Location,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  u.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate
FROM users u
views.description: Subset/cohort view exposing users and commonly filtered profile fields (name, location, creation and access dates) for filtering or display without sensitive columns.

views.name: user_badge_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count_total
FROM badges AS b
GROUP BY b.UserId
views.description: Badge counts per user (counts of badges by Name and total badges) to support comparisons and enriched ranking of users by recognition.

views.name: users_core_3
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(u.DisplayName, ''), up.DisplayName) AS DisplayName,
  up.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN users_public_profile up ON up.Id = u.Id
views.description: Canonical user row with core identity and temporal columns; cleans/normalizes fields used for filtering and display.

views.name: users_by_creation_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', u.CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS CreationYear
FROM users_public_profile u
views.description: User cohort augmented with the calendar year of their CreationDate for fast year-based filtering and grouping.

views.name: user_activity_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS UserId,
  COALESCE(p.PostCount, 0) AS PostCount,
  COALESCE(c.CommentCount, 0) AS CommentCount,
  COALESCE(b.badge_count_total, 0) AS BadgeCount,
  COALESCE(v.VoteCount, 0) AS VoteCount
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT OwnerUserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS PostCount
  FROM posts
  WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY OwnerUserId
) p ON p.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS CommentCount
  FROM comments
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) c ON c.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS VoteCount
  FROM votes
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) v ON v.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, badge_count_total
  FROM user_badge_counts
) b ON b.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Per-user aggregated activity counts (posts, comments, badges, votes) to support queries that filter or sort users by activity; counts are raw totals (no date filter).

views.name: users_core_6
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  u.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users AS u
views.description: Canonical user rows with key identity and principal timestamp/metadata normalized for filtering and reuse.
validated_on: How many posts does the user csgillespie own?

views.name: users_lastaccess_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate
FROM users u
WHERE u.LastAccessDate IS NOT NULL
views.description: Cohort of users with a non-null LastAccessDate, exposing the LastAccessDate for date-based cohorting (one row per user). Useful for counting active/recent users or applying date filters.

views.name: user_activity_summary_8
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(p.post_count, 0) AS post_count,
  COALESCE(a.answer_count, 0) AS answer_count,
  COALESCE(c.comment_count, 0) AS comment_count,
  COALESCE(b.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count,
  COALESCE(v.vote_count, 0) AS vote_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT OwnerUserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS post_count
  FROM posts
  WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY OwnerUserId
) p ON p.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT OwnerUserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS answer_count
  FROM posts
  WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL AND PostTypeId = 2
  GROUP BY OwnerUserId
) a ON a.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS comment_count
  FROM comments
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) c ON c.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS badge_count
  FROM badges
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) b ON b.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS vote_count
  FROM votes
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) v ON v.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Basic per-user activity summary aggregating counts/measures from related tables (posts, comments, badges, votes). One row per user with raw counts to support filters or group-bys in downstream questions.

views.name: posts_owner_display_and_user_ref
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  CASE
    WHEN posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL THEN posts.OwnerUserId
    WHEN posts.OwnerUserId IS NULL THEN NULL
  END AS OwnerUserId,
  NULLIF(TRIM(posts.OwnerDisplayName), '') AS OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts
views.description: Normalized projection of posts' owner identity capturing both the stored OwnerDisplayName (denormalized) and the canonical OwnerUserId for lookups; cleans empty strings to NULL.

views.name: posts_minimal_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts
views.description: Small selectable cohort of posts with core identity and ownership columns (keeps Title for exact-match filters).

views.name: users_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName
FROM users_core_6 u
views.description: Canonical user identity projection exposing user DisplayName for joining to posts when OwnerDisplayName is not present.

views.name: posts_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id,
  p.OwnerUserId,
  p.PostTypeId,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  p.Title
FROM posts p
views.description: Row-level view of posts exposing keys and ownership columns; one row per post to serve as the base cohort for counts, filters, and joins.

views.name: user_posts_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized rows joining posts to their owner user (exposes both post and owner user fields) to support queries that filter posts by user attributes.

views.name: posts_core_14
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  TRIM(posts.Title) AS Title,
  posts.LastEditorUserId AS LastEditorUserId
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post with canonicalized key columns and trimmed important attributes for filtering and joins (clean common misspellings).

views.name: posts_with_last_editor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.LastEditorUserId AS LastEditorUserId,
  u.DisplayName AS LastEditorDisplayName,
  CASE WHEN p.LastEditorUserId IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS LastEditorUserId_is_null
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u
  ON p.LastEditorUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to the user who last edited them (if any), one row per post with last editor info.

views.name: posts_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  CASE WHEN posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL THEN posts.OwnerUserId ELSE NULL END AS OwnerUserId,
  CASE WHEN posts.Score IS NOT NULL THEN posts.Score ELSE 0 END AS Score,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post with canonical cleaned columns useful for filtering and joining to users (casts/nullable canonicalization).

views.name: users_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.Age AS Age,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users u
views.description: One row per user exposing demographic and identity columns commonly used for filtering (age, reputation) and joining to posts and other artifacts.
validated_on: Which user made a post titled 'Understanding what Dassault iSight is doing?' and how much is the reputation of the user?

views.name: posts_with_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  p.Score AS Score,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.Tags AS Tags,
  u.Id AS Owner_Id,
  u.Age AS Owner_Age,
  u.Reputation AS Owner_Reputation,
  u.DisplayName AS Owner_DisplayName
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u
  ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized row-level view: one row per post enriched with its owner's core user attributes (age, reputation). Useful for questions that filter posts by owner properties.

views.name: tags_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  TagName AS TagName,
  Count AS Count,
  ExcerptPostId AS ExcerptPostId,
  WikiPostId AS WikiPostId
FROM tags
views.description: One-row-per-tag basic projection containing tag identifiers and the referenced post ids (excerpt and wiki) and counts.

views.name: posts_core_20
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostTypeId,
  AcceptedAnswerId,
  CreaionDate,
  Score,
  ViewCount,
  Body,
  OwnerUserId,
  LasActivityDate,
  Title,
  Tags,
  AnswerCount,
  CommentCount,
  FavoriteCount,
  ParentId,
  ClosedDate,
  OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post canonical projection exposing key post attributes used for lookups and content retrieval.

views.name: tag_excerpt_post_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tags.Id AS "tags.Id",
  tags.TagName AS "tags.TagName",
  tags.ExcerptPostId AS "tags.ExcerptPostId",
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.Body AS "posts.Body"
FROM tags AS tags
JOIN posts AS posts
  ON tags.ExcerptPostId = posts.Id
WHERE tags.ExcerptPostId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized relation joining tags to their excerpt post (when ExcerptPostId is present) so a query can directly retrieve the post content for a given tag name.

views.name: posts_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(posts.OwnerUserId, NULL) AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(posts.Score, 0) AS Score,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post with canonicalized key columns and core attributes used for filtering, grouping, and measures. Normalizes nullable numeric/text fields and exposes owner linkage.

views.name: posts_by_owner_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  p.Score AS Score,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  COALESCE(u.DisplayName, p.OwnerDisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u
  ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized per-post rows joined to their owner user row. Keeps one row per post with owner DisplayName and user id to make owner-level aggregations simple.

views.name: posts_core_24
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post core projection with canonical columns used for filtering and joins (keeps raw score and owner user id).

views.name: posts_with_owner_age
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  users.Age AS Age
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to the owner's user row (if any) exposing post fields plus owner Age for direct predicates like 'owned by elder users'.

views.name: comments_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.Score AS Score,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName,
  comments.Text AS Text
FROM comments
views.description: Row-level cohort of comments with their identifying and linking columns and timestamps. One row per comment; useful for filtering by commenter, time window, or related post.

Name the user that commented 'thank you user93!'

views.name: post_comments_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS "comments.Id",
  comments.PostId AS "comments.PostId",
  comments.UserId AS "comments.UserId",
  comments.CreationDate AS "comments.CreationDate",
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.FavoriteCount AS "posts.FavoriteCount"
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN posts ON comments.PostId = posts.Id
views.description: Denormalized relation joining comments to their posts (comment-level rows enriched with post attributes). One row per comment (joined to its post) to support queries that filter comments then return post measures.

views.name: posts_core_28
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  ClosedDate,
  Title,
  OwnerUserId,
  PostTypeId,
  ParentId
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical projection of posts exposing identity, owner, status and key datetime fields (ClosedDate) for determining whether a post is closed. Keeps the raw columns needed for status checks and joins.

views.name: comment_post_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS "comments.Id AS CommentId",
  comments.PostId AS "comments.PostId AS CommentPostId",
  comments.UserId AS "comments.UserId",
  comments.CreationDate AS "comments.CreationDate",
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id AS PostId",
  posts.ClosedDate AS "posts.ClosedDate"
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN posts ON posts.Id = comments.PostId
views.description: Denormalized join between comments and their parent posts, one row per comment, exposing both comment attributes and the post's ClosedDate so queries can directly test whether the commented-on post is closed.

views.name: posts_core_30
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post exposing ownership, title, and raw measures needed for counts and filtering (no aggregation).

views.name: user_posts_join_31
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.DisplayName AS "DisplayName as user_display_name",
  users.Id AS "Id as user_id",
  posts.Id AS "Id as post_id"
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized row-level relation: each row is a post joined to its owner user (if any). Exposes both user and post keys and the user's DisplayName for exact-match lookups and post-level analyses.

views.name: votes_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostId,
  VoteTypeId,
  CreationDate,
  UserId,
  BountyAmount
FROM votes
views.description: Row-level view of votes with core vote attributes for joining and filtering (one row per vote).

views.name: users_core_33
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  Reputation,
  AccountId
FROM users
views.description: Canonical projection of users with identifying/display fields used for answers and joins.
validated_on: Name the user that commented 'thank you user93!'

views.name: votes_with_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.Id,
  v.PostId,
  v.VoteTypeId,
  v.CreationDate,
  v.UserId,
  v.BountyAmount,
  u.DisplayName AS UserDisplayName
FROM votes AS v
LEFT JOIN users AS u
  ON v.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized join of votes to their casting user (left join votes -> users) producing one row per vote including user display name for easy lookup.

views.name: posts_by_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Score AS Score
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post cohort exposing post identity and ownership attributes for filtering, grouping, and counting of posts by owner.

views.name: user_post_vote_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS UserId,
  COALESCE(p.posts_count, 0) AS posts_count,
  COALESCE(v.votes_count, 0) AS votes_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT OwnerUserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS posts_count
  FROM posts
  WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY OwnerUserId
) p ON p.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS votes_count
  FROM votes
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) v ON v.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Per-user aggregated counts of posts owned and votes cast. Useful for computing ratios or per-user activity summaries.

views.name: posts_core_37
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of posts with primary identifying columns and common measures (score, view count, counts, owner and timestamps). Useful as the foundational posts row-level view for selection, filtering, and joins.

views.name: posts_with_owner_38
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Denormalized post rows joined to their owner user row to expose owner attributes alongside posts for filtering and aggregation by user properties.

views.name: post_title_indexable
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount
FROM posts
views.description: Lightweight view focusing on post id, exact Title, and ViewCount to support exact-title lookup and fast projection of view counts.

views.name: comments_with_post_and_user_ids
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS PostOwnerUserId,
  comments.Score AS Score,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN posts ON posts.Id = comments.PostId
views.description: Denormalized view linking comments to their post and commenter user ids and key timestamps; useful for filters that combine comment, post and user attributes.

views.name: comments_score_counts_per_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  COUNT(comments.Id) AS comment_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN comments.Score = 17 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS comments_with_score_17_count,
  AVG(CAST(comments.Score AS REAL)) AS avg_comment_score,
  MAX(comments.Score) AS max_comment_score
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN comments ON comments.PostId = posts.Id
GROUP BY posts.Id
views.description: Aggregated measures of comment counts and score distribution per post; one row per post useful for post-level filtering or ranking by comment counts or by comments with specific scores.

views.name: comment_user_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS CommentId,
  comments.Text AS CommentText,
  comments.CreationDate AS CommentCreationDate,
  comments.UserId AS CommentUserId,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName,
  users.DisplayName AS UserDisplayName_from_users,
  users.Reputation AS UserReputation
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN users ON comments.UserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized view joining comments to their authoring user (when present) to expose comment text alongside the author's DisplayName and user id — useful for lookups by comment text or author.

views.name: posts_row_level_43
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts
views.description: Normalized row-level representation of posts exposing identifying and commonly filtered columns (one row per post). Cleans/aliases original columns for consistent use in joins and filtering.

views.name: posts_with_owner_44
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  users.DisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS OwnerReputation
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized posts joined to their owner user (one row per post) to enable direct filtering by post attributes and returning owner fields without an extra join.

views.name: users_minimal
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(u.DisplayName, up.DisplayName) AS DisplayName
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN users_public_profile up ON up.Id = u.Id
views.description: One-row-per-user projection exposing user id and canonical display name for joins to posts owners.

views.name: post_owner_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  p.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  u.DisplayName AS UserDisplayName
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized one-row-per-post that brings together the post's owner user id, the post's stored OwnerDisplayName, and the canonical users.DisplayName when available.

views.name: posts_with_edit_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  CASE WHEN ph.PostId IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS HasEdits
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN postHistory ph ON ph.PostId = p.Id
GROUP BY p.Id, p.Title, p.OwnerUserId
views.description: One row per post with a boolean flag indicating whether the post has any postHistory (i.e. was edited).

views.name: comments_by_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName,
  posts.Title AS PostTitle
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN posts ON comments.PostId = posts.Id
views.description: All comments joined to their post identifiers and minimal post metadata; one row per comment.

views.name: post_history_by_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PostId,
  COUNT(Id) AS EditCount,
  MIN(CreationDate) AS FirstEditDate,
  MAX(CreationDate) AS LastEditDate
FROM postHistory
GROUP BY PostId
views.description: Aggregate counts and latest edit info for postHistory grouped by post. One row per post summarizing its edit activity.

views.name: posts_minimal
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  Title,
  OwnerUserId,
  PostTypeId,
  ParentId
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post exposing canonical identifying and text fields used for filtering or joining (title, owner, parent relationship, counts). Normalizes column name typos if necessary.

views.name: users_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  u.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users u
views.description: One row per user with primary identity attributes (display name, reputation, creation date) for reporting and joining to votes/posts.

views.name: posts_with_tags_and_basic_meta
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post exposing identifying columns and tag text for filtering and later joins. Keeps raw measures like ViewCount and Title for aggregation or projection.

views.name: posts_humor_cohort_for_aggregation
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount
FROM posts
WHERE posts.Tags = '<humor>'

semantic_filters.Tags: LIKE '%<humor>%'  -- this is shown as an intended filter, but actual literal should be applied in question_ops

views.description: Cohort of posts intended for computing aggregate measures over posts that have a particular tag. This view returns one row per post (no aggregation across posts) but is marked AGG to indicate it's used for aggregation in downstream queries. It exposes the raw ViewCount used to compute AVG(ViewCount) over the cohort.

views.name: badges_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UserId,
  Name,
  Date
FROM badges
WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.UserId: IS NOT NULL  -- keep only badges tied to a user when desired (can be relaxed later)

views.description: Canonical normalized view of the badges table: one row per badge event with key columns and cleaned/nullable fields exposed for downstream filtering and grouping.

views.name: badges_count_per_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(badges.Id) AS badge_count,
  MIN(badges.Date) AS first_badge_date,
  MAX(badges.Date) AS last_badge_date
FROM badges
WHERE badges.UserId IS NOT NULL  -- exclude anonymous/unlinked badge rows by default
GROUP BY badges.UserId

semantic_filters.UserId: IS NOT NULL  -- exclude anonymous/unlinked badge rows by default

views.description: Aggregated counts of badges per user. One row per badges.UserId with raw count of badge rows and (optionally) earliest/latest badge dates for that user.

views.name: users_with_badge_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  COALESCE(bc.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    UserId,
    COUNT(*) AS badge_count
  FROM badges
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) bc ON bc.UserId = u.Id
WHERE u.Id IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.Id: IS NOT NULL  -- ensure valid users only

views.description: Denormalized per-user summary joining users and aggregated badge counts: one row per users.Id with user metadata and badge_count for easy filtering and reporting.

views.name: posthistory_per_post_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  postHistory.PostId AS PostId,
  postHistory.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(postHistory.Id) AS history_count
FROM postHistory
WHERE postHistory.PostId IS NOT NULL
  AND postHistory.UserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY postHistory.PostId, postHistory.UserId
views.description: Counts postHistory rows grouped by PostId and UserId. One row per (PostId, UserId) pairing with the raw count of postHistory entries for that pairing.

views.name: users_with_highview_posts_and_history_check
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  posts.ViewCount AS "posts.ViewCount",
  COALESCE(ph_counts.history_count, 0) AS "postHistory_counts.history_count",
  users.Id AS "users.Id",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName"
FROM posts
JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    PostId,
    UserId,
    COUNT(*) AS history_count
  FROM postHistory
  GROUP BY PostId, UserId
) AS ph_counts
  ON ph_counts.PostId = posts.Id
  AND ph_counts.UserId = posts.OwnerUserId
WHERE posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized relation joining users -> posts (filtered to posts with high views) -> postHistory counts (per post,user). One row per post that has an owner: exposes whether that owner has exactly N history rows for that post. Useful to evaluate 'for every high-view post owned by a user, does that user have exactly k postHistory rows for that post'.

views.name: badges_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UserId,
  Name,
  Date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER) AS year
FROM badges
views.description: Canonical/clean row-level view of badges exposing badge id, user, name and a normalized year extracted from the Date column for easy yearly filtering and grouping.

views.name: badges_by_year_and_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.Id AS Id,
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  badges.Name AS Name,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY badges.Name, CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER)) AS badge_count
FROM badges
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of badges per badge Name and year (derived from Date). Useful for quickly computing shares of a badge name across years.

views.name: user_badge_counts_61
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  badges.Name AS Name,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count_by_user_name_year
FROM badges
GROUP BY
  badges.UserId,
  badges.Name,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Counts of badges per user and badge name, optionally broken out by year. One row per user + Name (+ optional year) to support per-user badge analyses and filtering/cohorting.

views.name: user_posts_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts
WHERE posts.Id IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per post, exposing post owner and post id so callers can form user-level cohorts by counting posts per user.

views.name: users_core_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.UpVotes AS UpVotes,
  u.Age AS Age
FROM users u
views.description: Canonical user-level projection exposing key demographic and reputation fields used in analytics (UpVotes, Age, Id). NULLs preserved so callers can exclude NULLs per-measure as needed.

views.name: users_post_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(p.Id) AS posts_count
FROM posts p
WHERE p.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.OwnerUserId
views.description: Per-user aggregated measure: number of posts authored by each user (counts posts where posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id).

views.name: votes_rowlevel_65
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostId,
  VoteTypeId,
  CreationDate,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS CreationYear,
  UserId,
  BountyAmount
FROM votes
views.description: Canonical row-level view of votes with normalized/date-extracted fields for downstream filtering and aggregation.

views.name: votes_counts_by_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  COUNT(*) AS vote_count
FROM votes
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregated counts of votes per year (year extracted from CreationDate). Keeps one row per year to support year-over-year comparisons.

views.name: post_votes_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.Id,
  v.PostId,
  v.VoteTypeId,
  v.CreationDate,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', v.CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS CreationYear,
  v.UserId,
  v.BountyAmount,
  p.Title AS "posts.Title",
  p.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  p.Tags AS "posts.Tags",
  p.PostTypeId AS "posts.PostTypeId"
FROM votes AS v
LEFT JOIN posts AS p
  ON v.PostId = p.Id
views.description: Denormalized relation joining votes to posts to expose post-level dimensions (owner, tags, title) alongside vote rows for analyses that correlate votes with post attributes.

views.name: posts_by_id
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical post rows with primary metadata and counts; one row per post (exposes owner and answer/comment counts for filtering/ordering).

views.name: posts_with_owner_displayname
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(users.DisplayName, posts.OwnerDisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to their owner's user display name to enable author-based filtering and ranking by post metrics.

views.name: posts_row_level_70
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount
FROM posts
views.description: Row-level view of the posts table exposing the key identifiers and raw measures (no aggregation). NULL ViewCount left as-is for normalization later.

views.name: posts_owner_viewcount_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(posts.OwnerDisplayName, ''), users.DisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName,
  COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0) AS ViewCount_norm
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Canonical projection of post owner identity and cleaned view count: ensures OwnerDisplayName and a numeric ViewCount (NULL -> 0). Useful for author-level aggregations.

views.name: author_total_views
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  OwnerDisplayName,
  SUM(COALESCE(ViewCount, 0)) AS TotalViewCount
FROM posts
GROUP BY OwnerDisplayName
views.description: Pre-aggregated total view counts per author display name, summing view counts across their posts. NULL ViewCount treated as 0 in the aggregation. This is a general author popularity measure that can be filtered/ordered later.
